named_subject: a skateboard (long tilted deck on two round wheels)
action: The board rolls down and to the left toward the viewer, tilting nose-down to the right and growing larger through frame 6, then shrinks and moves back up in frames 7-8.
identity_gap: In c.png the two wheels are closed, solid polygons with the left wheel's stroke running up into the deck; in many animated frames the wheels are open hooks, drop away from the deck, or carry stray cross marks (frames 4 and 6), and the right wheel in frame 7 becomes a trailing tail. The deck in c.png is a fat rounded slab, while the animated deck is a thinner slanted sliver.
notes: The scale jumps from frame 5 to 6 and back down at 8, and the wheels detach and change shape from frame to frame, which reads as popping rather than rolling. The change that would help most is to keep both wheels as closed shapes rigidly attached under the deck, so only the whole drawing tilts, moves and scales smoothly.
_repair: wheels no longer spin; board length held steady
